title: chore(scripts): ten ratchet baselines become one-sided — a decrease passes and is reported
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9MprVKsmUWQJJ3yeQLxiEMG)_
Part of #26444
Part of #26431

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

The devx half of #26444 only. The ui floors are #26521 and the CLI floors are #26523, so this PR does not close the card.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：10 个棘轮读者(slot-lookup、query-options-erasure、role-word、i18n-coverage、corpus-claim-drift、objectql-double-limit、where-matcher、optional-error-sink、durability 两本账、published-readme-exports)从「两侧」改成「单侧」：基线里的数减少或文件被删 → 通过，并在输出里报告;增加或新文件 → 照旧变红。空扫描仍然变红：基线里列着、文件还在磁盘上、这次却没读到，就拒绝(第一轮席位复核加的)。
- 为什么改：删一个文件或修好一处，就要跑 `--update` 才能过 CI，跟这个 PR 的工作无关;卡 #26444 的 Wanted 3。
- 风险与回滚：代价是「余量」。减少后没跑 `--update`，旧数仍是上限，可以悄悄补回同样多的违例;每条报告都写明了余量。回滚就是 revert 本 PR，没有数据或接线变化。
- 先看：`scripts/check-query-options-erasure-ratchet.mjs`(唯一带聚合上限的一本)、`scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs`(比较逻辑抽成纯函数)、`scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs`(两本账共用的 reconcileLedger)。
- 两分钟验证：`rm content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx && node scripts/check-role-word.mjs; echo $?; git checkout HEAD -- content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`，应看到 `1 baselined file(s) improved (passing, reported)`，退出码 0。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

Each reader keeps its error path for the increase direction and gains a pure, separately-named decrease report:

| Reader | Baseline | Decrease (now passes, printed on stdout) | Self-test |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `check-slot-lookup-ratchet.mjs` | `slot-lookup-baseline.json` | `ratchetDownReport()` | battery 3 floor 6 → 11 |
| `check-query-options-erasure-ratchet.mjs` | `query-options-erasure-baseline.json` (per-file + `testSurface` aggregate) | `ratchetDownReport()` (exported beside `diffRatchet`) | battery 2 floor 8 → 15 |
| `check-role-word.mjs` | `role-word-baseline.json` | `ratchetVerdict().down` | new battery (7), roster floor 14 → 15 |
| `check-i18n-coverage.mjs` | `i18n-coverage-baseline.json` | `ratchetVerdict().down` (comparison lifted out of the top level) | new battery (6), roster floor 6 → 7 |
| `check-corpus-claim-drift.mjs` | `corpus-claim-drift-baseline.json` | `ratchetVerdict().down` | new battery (7), roster floor 17 → 18 |
| `check-objectql-double-limit.mjs` | `objectql-double-limit.baseline.json` | `reconcileDown()` | battery floor 47 → 52 |
| `check-where-matcher-conformance.mjs` | `where-matcher-conformance.baseline.json` | `reconcileDown()` | new battery (5), roster floor 3 → 4 |
| `check-optional-error-sink-contract.mjs` | `optional-error-sink-contract.baseline.json` | `reconcileLedger().stale` | floor 66 → 70 |
| `check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` | `durability-degradation.baseline.json`, `durability-read-invention.baseline.json` | `reconcileLedger().stale` (shared by both rules) | one row per partition; floors 68/57/125 → 69/58/127 |
| `check-published-readme-exports.mjs` | `published-readme-exports.baseline.json` | stale entries printed on stdout; exit 0 | new end-to-end battery (3) on the scratch workspace, roster floor 27 → 28 |

Every decrease line names its headroom: the old number stays the ceiling, or the stale key keeps licensing that site, until `--update` (or the hand edit, for the two gates with no `--update`) records it. `--update` is unchanged and remains the way to write the report down.

Kept as errors on purpose:
- A NEW file or key, and a grown count (the defect each gate exists for).
- Every key-set monotonicity check ("ADDED to the baseline").
- corpus-claim-drift: a ledger row naming a rule `VOCABULARY` no longer holds. That is an unfinished retirement, not a decrease.

The `$comment` headers of the seven baselines that described two-sided reconciliation now describe the one-sided one. Only `$comment` text changed; no counts or keys moved.

## Premise, measured on `origin/main` b7f2b0c2 before the change

All ten readers were two-sided, and none was already one-sided. A real deletion of a listed file, run on the base tree, went red:

| Gate | Deletion on base | Exit |
|:---|:---|:---|
| role-word | `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` | 1 (`baselined file is clean/gone … ratchet DOWN`) |
| corpus-claim-drift | `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx` | 1 (`improved 1 → 0 … ratchet DOWN`) |
| objectql-double-limit | `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-drafts-advisories.test.ts` | 1 (`clean or gone -- ratchet DOWN`) |
| optional-error-sink | `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts` | 1 (`stale entry … shrink-only`) |
| durability (both ledgers) | stale entry injected (simulates a gone file) | 1 each |
| where-matcher | stale entry injected (the ledger is empty) | 1 (`clean or gone` + `ADDED`) |
| slot-lookup, query-options | base self-test cases `a fall must be ratcheted down` / `a cleaned file must be dropped` assert 1 error | read off the pure `diffRatchet` |
| i18n-coverage, published-readme-exports | code read: decrease / stale branch pushes an error and exits 1 | not run on base (build needed) |

## Acceptance: deleting a listed file reds no ratchet; a new violation still reds

Run on head `60e74485`, after the dead-scan round. The first run, on `c4087da0`, gave the same exits. Each mutation is applied, the gate runs, then the tree is restored with `git checkout HEAD --` plus removal of new files, and the restore is checked with `git status` (clean every time).

| Gate | DOWN: deleted a listed file → exit | UP: added a violation → exit |
|:---|:---|:---|
| role-word | `error-catalog.mdx` removed → **0**, reported | one more "role" in the same page → **1** |
| corpus-claim-drift | `http-protocol.mdx` removed → **0**, reported | duplicated the claim line → **1** |
| objectql-double-limit | `protocol-publish-drafts-advisories.test.ts` removed → **0**, reported | copied it to a new path → **1** (NEW) |
| where-matcher | ledger is empty, so no real deletion is possible; self-test only | new test file (copied from a fixture) with an early-return matcher → **1** (NEW) |
| optional-error-sink | `settings-service.types.ts` removed → **0**, stale reported | new `interface { error?: … }` → **1** |
| durability (log-level) | stale entry injected → **0**, reported | new catch around `syncSchema` logging `warn` → **1** |
| durability (read invention) | stale entry injected → **0**, reported | (the UP above runs both rules in one process) |
| slot-lookup | `packages/core/examples/kernel-features-example.ts` removed → **0**, reported | one more `getService<any>` in that file → **1** |
| query-options-erasure | `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` removed → **0**, reported | one more `query as any` in that file → **1** |
| i18n-coverage | `examples/app-todo/objectstack.config.ts` removed → **0**, reported | one `zh-CN` label line deleted → **1** |
| published-readme-exports | ledger is empty, so a stale entry was injected → **0**, reported | an invented import in `packages/spec/README.md` → **1** |

## Dead scans stay red (seat review, round 1)

When the ratchets were two-sided, a scan that lost part of its population dropped those baselined entries out of the measurement, and the DOWN direction went red once per entry. Now that the ratchets are one-sided, that same drop would read as a passing decrease. So the gate now asks the scan itself: if a baselined entry is still **on disk** but the run did not read it, the gate refuses. A deleted file is not on disk, and a swept file was read, so both still pass. The table lists, for each reader, what reds a scan or walk that read nothing. "New" marks a refusal added in this round. Each new refusal has self-test cases, and one of them is an empty population.

| Reader | What reds a scan that read nothing | New self-test |
|:---|:---|:---|
| role-word | missing ROOT (existing, #9932); **new:** a baselined page on disk that the walk did not read | battery (7), including two spawned legs: a ledgered page parked in a skipped subtree exits 1, and the same entry with the page deleted exits 0 |
| corpus-claim-drift | missing ROOT (existing); a scan that read nothing also leaves every VOCABULARY row unreachable (existing); **new:** a baselined page on disk that the walk did not read | battery (5) |
| slot-lookup | ESLint throws on a target that matches no file; the rule-gone and rescoped refusals (existing); **new:** a baselined file on disk that the rule did not run on (not linted, or its `ignores` not lifted, read from `calculateConfigForFile`) | battery 6 (7), including two live legs: with the ignore left in place the resolved config has no rule, and with it lifted the resolved config has the rule |
| query-options-erasure | the same ESLint and rule-gone guards (existing); **new:** a baselined non-test file the rule did not run on; **new:** the test surface measuring 0 against a non-zero ceiling | battery 6 (8) |
| i18n-coverage | zero configs refused, exit 3 (existing, #10907); **new:** a baselined config on disk that the round did not measure; **new:** every measured config reading 0 while the ledger still holds strings (`os lint` renamed its `i18n/` rules, or the classifier went blind) | battery (6) |
| objectql-double-limit | DISCOVERED: zero graded doubles (existing); **new:** a baselined file on disk that the corpus walk never read | 4 cases |
| where-matcher-conformance | DISCOVERED: zero matchers found (existing). The ledger is empty, so there is no row a partial scan could turn into a decrease. | none (unchanged) |
| optional-error-sink | **new:** no source file read, no sink declaring `error` found at all, or a ledgered file on disk the walk never reached. Before this round nothing caught it: a dead scan reported all five rows as stale and passed. | 5 cases |
| durability (both ledgers) | a scan that read nothing leaves FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES / READ_FAILURE_DISCRIMINATORS stale, which still reds (existing, left two-sided); **new:** a ledgered file on disk the walk never read | one row per partition |
| published-readme-exports | DOCUMENTS = 0 and the other population refusals (existing, self-tested) | none (unchanged) |

No floor was introduced, so none rots on the next `--update`. Each refusal checks an identity (on disk and not read) or a zero.

There are two places where a legitimate final sweep is refused until `--update` records it. The message names that remedy, and the zero ceiling that `--update` writes disarms the refusal:
- i18n-coverage, when the last untranslated strings in every measured config are translated in one round.
- query-options, when the last test-code erasure is swept.

Deleting a file never trips either refusal.

Dead-scan demos on `60e74485`. In each one, the gate's own walk or lift was broken for a single run, the gate was run, and the file was restored with `git checkout HEAD --` and a clean `git status`:

| Gate | Mutation (script only) | Exit |
|:---|:---|:---|
| role-word | `content/docs/api` added to SKIP_SUBTREES | **1**, names the 2 ledgered pages it did not read |
| corpus-claim-drift | `content/docs/protocol/kernel` added to SKIP_SUBTREES | **1**, names `http-protocol.mdx` |
| slot-lookup | the measuring config lifts no `ignores` | **2**, 25 baselined files the rule did not run on |
| query-options | the same, for its non-test run | **2**, 15 files |
| query-options | the test globs not lifted | **2**, test surface 0 against a ceiling of 236 |
| i18n-coverage | the classifier matches `i18nx/` instead of `i18n/` | **1**, every config at 0 against 527 |
| optional-error-sink | SCAN_ROOTS pointed at a missing directory | **1**, no source file read |
| objectql-double-limit | the walk skips `metadata-protocol` | **1**, UNREAD: 49 baselined files |
| durability (read invention) | `packages/objectql/src` dropped from the read-seam roots | **1**, names `engine.ts` |

## Tests

- `--self-test` of all ten readers: exit 0, each carrying its new decrease-passes and increase-reds cases (table above).
- Production run of all ten readers on head: exit 0.
- No package test exercises these scripts. The 15 `*.test.ts` files that name one of them only mention it in comments; those were read and none asserts behaviour this PR changes.

## Acceptance notes

- **Headroom is the stated cost.** A one-sided ratchet left above reality licenses that many new sites until someone runs `--update`. The decrease report names the number on every run. The query-options test-surface line spells out `licenses N new test-code erasure(s)`.
- **The detector-weakening signal moved to the self-tests.** A rule narrowed so far that live counts fall used to red the production run of slot-lookup, query-options and i18n-coverage. It now prints decrease reports. The self-tests, which drive the real rule over synthetic sources in both directions, are now the only thing that catches it. The slot-lookup header and the i18n classifier comment say this.
- **eslint-ignore couplings (slot-lookup, query-options), re-read as the card asked.** The baseline keys are still the `ignores` of their `eslint.config.mjs` blocks, and both ratchets still measure listed files with the ignore lifted, so growth in a listed file stays red. A key whose file is gone stays an `ignores` glob until `--update` drops it, which does no harm. If a file is later recreated at that same path, it rides the stale count. The report says to drop the entry.
- **Keyed ledgers** (optional-error-sink, both durability ledgers, readme-exports): a stale row re-licenses that exact key until it is deleted. The report says so.
- Not touched: `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (no step's invocation changed). Its comment at line 4209 still calls the query-options test count "decrease-only". It is a governed file and only a comment.
- Left two-sided, outside this card's list: `engine-double-contract.baseline.json` and `startup-registry-verdict.baseline.json` (both still fail on a stale entry), and the durability vocabulary staleness checks (`FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES`, `READ_FAILURE_DISCRIMINATORS`), which are declarations rather than baselines.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.metadata-store-outage.test.ts:636-639` has a comment saying the durability ledger and code are "pinned to each other in both directions". Only the restored-limb direction still reds. This is a comment outside the file surface, so it is left alone.

## Verification

<details><summary>Derived gate families — 41/41 exit 0 on 60e74485 (and on c4087da0 before it), --ran reconciliation 0 NOT-MEASURED</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 41 families, and each was run with its exit captured before any pipe. `pnpm check:entry-guard` first went red, because `reconcileLedger` was exported from a file with an unguarded top level. The function was made module-private (commit c4087da0), and the gate then exited 0. `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` and `pnpm check:published-readme-exports` ran after a full `pnpm build` under `os-verify-lock`.

After the dead-scan round, the same 41 families were derived again (the set was unchanged) and run again on `60e74485`, and all 41 exited 0. On that head, `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran FILE` printed: `41 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 41 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero …)`.

</details>

<details><summary>Changeset</summary>

Repository tooling only: `scripts/*.mjs` and `scripts/*.json`. No published package's `files[]` ships them, so this PR is labelled `skip-changeset`.

</details>
